rounds.proof_sketch: Original: (256 + 256 - 1) / 256 = 1. Mutated: (256 + 1 - 1) / 256 = 1. Both equal 1 because 256 is exactly divisible by 256. The ceiling vs floor distinction only matters when dim1 % blockDim.x != 0.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the ceiling division formula ceil(dim1/blockDim.x) to floor(dim1/blockDim.x). With fixed shape [16, 256, 256], dim1=256 and blockDim.x=256. Since 256 is exactly divisible by 256, both ceiling and floor operations yield 1. This means elements_per_thread=1 in both cases, and each of the 256 threads processes exactly one element, covering all dim1 elements correctly. The mutation would cause incorrect behavior only if dim1 was not divisible by blockDim.x (e.g., dim1=257 or dim1=255), but this cannot occur under the fixed input shape contract.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed shape. Would require dim1 != blockDim.x or dim1 not divisible by blockDim.x to expose the ceiling vs floor difference.
rounds.recommendations: When testing GPU kernels with work distribution logic using ceiling division, ensure test shapes include non-divisible dimension sizes (e.g., dim1=257 or dim1=255 vs block_size=256) to catch mutations that break the ceiling division idiom.
